decisions.thought: Ting-Lu comfortably survives any unboosted attack from lead Hisuian Samurott. Establishing Stealth Rock immediately is the highest-value play, trading hazards even if Samurott uses Ceaseless Edge.

Turn 1 vs Ting-Lu, a hazard setter that will likely Spikes/Stealth Rock or Whirlwind. Samurott-H outspeeds (295 vs base 45) and Razor Shell with Sharpness (75×1.5 = ~112 BP) hits Ting-Lu's Ground typing for super effective damage — roughly 40-50% on physically bulky Ting-Lu. Ceaseless Edge sets Spikes but Dark is resisted by Ting-Lu. Razor Shell also has a Def-drop chance. Focus Sash keeps me alive against Earthquake. Ogerpon-Wellspring is a fine alternative, but taking the immediate damage on the lead is strongest; Ting-Lu can't threaten a KO through Sash. No Tera needed.

Ting-Lu is at 51% with -1 Def after my Razor Shell last turn. Razor Shell (Sharpness boosted, 112.5 BP, Water, super effective vs Ground) already took ~49% and dropped Def; another one at -1 Def easily KOs, even through Leftovers. Ting-Lu may switch out to a Water resist, but Razor Shell still does solid damage to most switch-ins, and I outspeed anyway (295 vs base 45). Ceaseless Edge would set Spikes but likely fails to KO. Razor Shell is the highest-value play; no need to Tera.

Ting-Lu is in KO range after the Defense drop, so preserving it is preferable. Dragonite is the safest pivot: it resists Razor Shell, keeps Multiscale through Stealth Rock with Heavy-Duty Boots, and can threaten setup or recovery next turn.

Dragonite at 89% with -1 Def (my Razor Shell dropped it). Dragonite likely Multiscale is broken (took damage). It threatens Extreme Speed or Dragon Dance. My Samurott (295 Spe) outspeeds base 80 Dragonite unboosted. Ceaseless Edge sets Spikes and does solid damage against -1 Def; Razor Shell hits harder. Dragonite likely DDs or Extreme Speeds; I have Focus Sash intact (no hazard damage taken yet? Stealth Rock is on my side but Samurott appears full HP so sash intact). Best play: Ceaseless Edge to stack Spikes for chip while dealing ~35-40% to -1 Def Dragonite. If it DDs, Sucker Punch next turn finishes. Spikes also punish Ting-Lu switches. No Tera needed.

Dragonite’s Multiscale is broken and Razor Shell has already dropped its Defense. Roost restores Multiscale while Dragon typing still resists Water, preventing Samurott from exploiting the defense drop and preserving Dragonite as a win condition.

Dragonite at 76% with -1 Def, likely Multiscale broken already. Dragonite's typical set: Dragon Dance, Extreme Speed, Earthquake/Fire Punch, Roost. Samurott-H outspeeds base 80 Dragonite (unless it has DD boosts; no boosts shown). Ceaseless Edge into -1 Def Dragonite does solid damage (~45-55%) and stacks another Spikes layer, punishing Ting-Lu switch-ins. Razor Shell is stronger (75 BP with Sharpness) but Dragonite resists Water? No—Dragon resists Water, so Razor Shell is resisted. Ceaseless Edge is neutral and adds hazards. Knock Off would reveal/remove item (Heavy-Duty Boots likely), but Ceaseless Edge with extra Spikes is better tempo. Focus Sash protects me from a surprise KO. Go Ceaseless Edge, no Tera needed.

Dragonite is the only hazard-immune Water resist and can survive either revealed attack even at -1 Defense. Roost restores it near full while scouting Samurott-H’s choice; switching risks heavy hazard chip or a super-effective Razor Shell into Great Tusk/Ting-Lu.

Dragonite is slower and at -1 Defense, making another Razor Shell dangerously costly. Great Tusk resists Ceaseless Edge, survives Razor Shell comfortably, activates Booster Energy, and can threaten Samurott while removing Spikes next turn.

Dragonite at 54% with -1 Def, likely Multiscale broken. Samurott-Hisui outspeeds (295 vs Dragonite's ~80 base, even Scarf is unlikely given Roost). Dragonite probably has Dragon Dance/Extreme Speed; it may Roost or set up. Ceaseless Edge with Sharpness (65×1.5=97.5 BP) into -1 Def Dragonite with no Multiscale does heavy damage and stacks a second Spikes layer. Razor Shell is slightly stronger (75×1.5) but Ceaseless Edge adds hazard value and Dark is neutral either way. Damage: ~50-60% on -1 Def Dragonite, likely KO or leaving it near death before it can Roost. Focus Sash protects against a surprise Extreme Speed/Outrage KO. No Tera needed.

Great Tusk at 67% HP, likely bulky. Samurott-H outspeeds Great Tusk (295 vs max ~289 base 87 with Jolly... actually Jolly Tusk hits 291, so it's close; but most Tusk are bulky or Adamant). Razor Shell is super effective and Sharpness-boosted: 75×1.5 = 112.5 BP Water STAB vs Ground. Adamant Samurott Razor Shell does roughly 60-70% to bulky Tusk, likely KOing from 67% or leaving it in Sucker Punch range. Tusk threatens Close Combat/Headlong Rush to OHKO, but Focus Sash is intact (though Stealth Rock on my side... Samurott is at full HP so Sash still works if not chipped—it wasn't hit by rocks since it's at 100%). Even if Tusk outspeeds, Sash guarantees I survive and fire off Razor Shell. Good line; no Tera needed.
Great Tusk naturally outspeeds Hisuian Samurott, and STAB super-effective Close Combat cleanly threatens the knockout, preventing another Ceaseless Edge layer. Terastallization is unnecessary.
Dragonite takes no entry-hazard damage thanks to Heavy-Duty Boots and can guarantee the revenge kill with +2 priority Extreme Speed, moving before any possible Aqua Jet.
Samurott-Hisui is at 1% and may outspeed Dragonite. Extreme Speed safely removes it before another Ceaseless Edge can add hazards; Terastallization is unnecessary.

Samurott-Hisui is at 1 HP and will die to any attack. Dragonite at 54% likely has Multiscale broken (it's damaged), so a Sucker Punch at 70 BP with Sharpness doesn't apply (not slicing), but still does decent damage. Dragonite likely outspeeds only if it has Dragon Dance boosts or Extreme Speed. Extreme Speed (+2 priority) beats Sucker Punch (+1), killing me before I move. However, Samurott is essentially dead anyway — getting value from it is the goal. Sucker Punch is the only way to attack before Dragonite moves (unless E-Speed). If Dragonite Roosts, Sucker Punch fails, but I then get a free Ceaseless Edge... no, I'd die to any hit next turn regardless. Switching wastes the sack — Samurott at 1 HP has no future use except chip. Best value: Sucker Punch for chip damage (~30%) on a 54% Dragonite, possibly threatening a later Kingambit Sucker Punch KO. If Dragonite E-Speeds, nothing lost that wouldn't be lost anyway.

Samurott fainted; must switch into Dragonite at 54% with Roost/Extreme Speed, likely Dragon Dance. Kingambit resists Extreme Speed (Steel) and gets Supreme Overlord boost (1 fainted ally). Kowtow Cleave threatens Dragonite heavily, and Sucker Punch outprioritizes Extreme Speed? No—Extreme Speed is +2, Sucker Punch +1. Still, Kingambit takes Extreme Speed comfortably and Iron Head deals big damage; Dragonite at 54% likely lacks Multiscale intact. Gholdengo also resists Extreme Speed and outspeeds unboosted Dragonite with Scarf, Make It Rain likely KOs at 54%, but if Dragonite has DD and Earthquake, risky. Kingambit is safest pivot: resists ESpeed, Lum Berry, and pressures Dragonite and Ting-Lu. Stealth Rock chip is fine.

Dragonite at 54% with Roost/Extreme Speed. Kingambit has Supreme Overlord boost (1 fainted ally, +10%). Kowtow Cleave (85 BP, ~1.1x boost) vs Dragonite: Kingambit's 405 Atk with Kowtow does roughly 45-55% to standard Dragonite — likely a KO or near-KO at 54%, especially if Multiscale is broken (it is, at 54%). Extreme Speed does little to Kingambit (Steel resists Normal). Dragonite might Dragon Dance/Earthquake, but Iron Head does more type-wise? Iron Head is neutral, Kowtow Cleave is neutral too; Kowtow has higher BP and never misses. If Dragonite Roosts, it becomes Dragon-only for the turn but still neutral to Dark. Kowtow Cleave is the straightforward play, keeping Tera in reserve.

Roost restores Dragonite to full before the slower Kingambit moves, reactivating Multiscale and sharply reducing any immediate attack. This preserves Dragonite while scouting whether Kingambit attacks, uses Swords Dance, or Terastallizes; Earthquake does not currently threaten an OHKO.

Dragonite at 73% with Roost/Extreme Speed. Kingambit with 1 fallen ally (Supreme Overlord +10%) has 405 Atk. Dragonite likely Multiscale broken (73%). Kowtow Cleave does ~45-55% to standard Dragonite; Iron Head similar but neutral. Dragonite's Extreme Speed doesn't OHKO Kingambit; Earthquake would hurt but Kingambit survives one from 94%.

Swords Dance is tempting but Dragonite could Dragon Dance too and set up; safer to just apply damage. Kowtow Cleave hits harder than Iron Head (85 BP vs 80, both neutral, Kowtow can't miss). Dragonite might Roost—Kowtow still forces roost loops with Stealth Rock/Spikes not affecting our attack. Chip it into Sucker Punch range next turn.

Choose Kowtow Cleave, no Tera needed.

Earthquake is the strongest immediate hit and exploits Kingambit’s 4× Ground weakness. Dragon Dance risks being punished by Kowtow Cleave followed by Sucker Punch, while switching forfeits valuable pressure.
Dragonite outspeeds standard Kingambit, and Earthquake comfortably KOs from 22%. Extreme Speed is resisted and may fail to finish it, while switching sacrifices immediate removal.

Dragonite at 15% with Extreme Speed (+2 priority) outspeeds Sucker Punch (+1). Kingambit at 21% (72 HP) — Extreme Speed from Dragonite (134 base Atk, possibly boosted) likely KOs or comes close; neutral on Dark/Steel, 80 BP. Risky. If Dragonite Roosts instead, Sucker Punch fails. Kowtow Cleave at 15% Dragonite definitely KOs if Kingambit survives, but Dragonite moves first with ESpeed.

Dragonite ESpeed: ~134 base Atk vs 277 Def, 80 BP neutral — roughly 25-30% of Kingambit, i.e., ~85-100 damage, exceeding 72 HP. Kingambit likely dies before attacking.

Better: switch to Gholdengo — immune to Extreme Speed (Ghost), resists nothing from EQ though (Steel/Ghost takes 2x from Ground). But Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds and Shadow Ball/Make It Rain KOs 15% Dragonite next turn, and Good as Gold blocks nothing relevant. If they Roost, Gholdengo still outspeeds unboosted Dragonite. If they EQ predicting Ghost, Gholdengo takes big damage but survives (100% HP). Alternatively Ogerpon-Wellspring: resists EQ? No, Grass/Water takes neutral Ground, resists Water only. Gholdengo's ESpeed immunity is the key value—Dragonite most likely clicks ESpeed to finish Kingambit.

Switch to Gholdengo.

Gholdengo fainted; I must switch in. Dragonite is at 15% with Extreme Speed (+2 priority) and Roost. Stealth Rock is on my side, so any switch-in takes chip.

Kingambit at 21% takes 12.5% from rocks, leaving ~8%; Extreme Speed likely KOs it — bad. Ribombee's Focus Sash breaks on rocks — wasteful. Ogerpon-Wellspring takes 6% from rocks, outspeeds Dragonite (350 vs base 80), but Extreme Speed is priority and Ivy Cudgel (Water) is resisted by Dragonite; Dragonite might be Multiscale-broken already though, so Ivy Cudgel would still KO 15%.

Iron Valiant: takes 6% from rocks, Booster Energy activates Speed (or SpA), Extreme Speed does ~35% to it. Moonblast is 4x... actually 2x vs Dragon/Flying and easily KOs 15% even through Roost. Also Encore can lock Roost. Iron Valiant is bulkier vs Extreme Speed than Kingambit and doesn't lose a Sash. Even if Dragonite Roosts, Moonblast next turn still likely KOs from ~65%.

Ogerpon is also fine, but Iron Valiant's Moonblast is super-effective and threatens Ting-Lu with Close Combat/Moonblast afterwards too.

Iron Valiant threatens an immediate Fairy-type knockout, while Dragonite cannot meaningfully threaten it from 94% with Extreme Speed. Gholdengo resists both Fairy and Fighting STAB and is the safest defensive pivot.

Dragonite at 15% HP. Extreme Speed (+2 priority) threatens Iron Valiant: 134 base Atk, 80 BP, but Iron Valiant at 271/289 easily survives Extreme Speed even boosted (Dragonite hasn't revealed Dragon Dance; ~35-45% damage max). Iron Valiant outspeeds anything except priority. Moonblast (339 SpA, 95 BP, resisted by Dragon? No — Fairy is neutral vs Dragon/Flying) easily KOs 15% Dragonite even if Multiscale were intact (it isn't at 15%). Any attack KOs; Moonblast is safest (no Def drops, no miss). If Dragonite Roosts, Moonblast still KOs since Valiant is faster. No Tera needed.
Iron Valiant outspeeds, but Gholdengo resists Moonblast and can immediately KO the specially frail Valiant with STAB Make It Rain. Terastallization is unnecessary and should be preserved.

Iron Valiant outspeeds Gholdengo (364 vs ~84 base). Gholdengo at 74% is Steel/Ghost — Shadow Ball is super effective (2x), Close Combat is neutral (Steel resists Fighting? No — Ghost is immune to Fighting). So Shadow Ball is the only strong option. 339 SpA Shadow Ball SE on Gholdengo: roughly 60-70% damage, likely leaving it low but possibly not KOing from 74%. Tera Ghost Shadow Ball would boost to ~90-105%, likely KOing. Alternatively, Tera Fairy Moonblast is resisted. Gholdengo threatens Valiant with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball (Valiant's SpD is low, 156), and Valiant likely dies to Make It Rain. Given Valiant outspeeds and Gholdengo is a key remaining threat (opponent has only Ting-Lu 51% and Dragonite 15% left), securing the KO now is decisive. Tera Ghost Shadow Ball is the highest-probability KO; without Tera it may fall short. Use Tera Ghost Shadow Ball.

Iron Valiant fainted; I need a replacement against Gholdengo at 14% (-1 SpA). Opponent has Gholdengo, Ting-Lu (51%), Dragonite (15%) left. I have Ribombee, Kingambit (21%), Ogerpon-Wellspring.

Kingambit at 21% with Stealth Rock takes 12.5% → ~8.6% left, too fragile; Gholdengo's Make It Rain kills it. Save Kingambit for Sucker Punch later (though Gholdengo's Good as Gold doesn't block attacks).

Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds Gholdengo (350 vs base 84) and Ivy Cudgel (Water, crit-boosted) or Horn Leech easily KOs Gholdengo at 14%. Even after Stealth Rock damage (12.5%), Ogerpon at ~87% threatens Ting-Lu with Ivy Cudgel (Water vs Ground) and Dragonite at 15% with anything. Make It Rain at -1 on Ogerpon won't OHKO. Ribombee's Sash is broken by rocks, making it less useful.

Ogerpon-Wellspring is the clear switch.

Gholdengo is at 14% and Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds it (350 vs base 84). Ivy Cudgel (Water-type with Wellspring Mask, 100 BP) will easily KO Gholdengo from 14% even though it's resisted by Steel? Actually Ivy Cudgel here is listed as Grass, but with Wellspring Mask it becomes Water — neutral on Steel/Ghost. Even Grass Horn Leech resisted would likely KO at 14%. Ivy Cudgel has high crit rate and 100% accuracy, guaranteed KO before Gholdengo can Make It Rain. Play Rough is resisted and 90% accurate — worse. Swords Dance risks taking Make It Rain. Just attack.
Gholdengo is outsped and KOed by Ogerpon. Dragapult safely resists both STABs, outspeeds Ogerpon, and preserves momentum with a strong Choice Specs attack next turn.

Dragapult at 12% outspeeds Ogerpon (base 142 vs my 350 speed — Dragapult with 142 base likely ~379+). It could Dragon Dart/Draco Meteor me, but Ogerpon at 88% survives most hits. Key: any attack KOs Dragapult. Ivy Cudgel is Grass and resisted by Dragon (0.5x) — Dragapult is Dragon/Ghost, so Grass is neutral... actually Grass vs Dragon is 0.5x, vs Ghost neutral = 0.5x. Even resisted, 100 BP Water-type Ivy Cudgel? No—Wellspring's Ivy Cudgel is Water-type, which is also resisted by Dragon. At 12% HP, even resisted Ivy Cudgel with 339 Atk easily KOs (Dragapult 75 base Def). Play Rough is neutral but 90% accuracy. Ivy Cudgel is 100% accurate with high crit and KOs a 12% Dragapult regardless. Switching to Kingambit for Sucker Punch is unnecessary risk. Attack with Ivy Cudgel.

Dragapult outspeeds Ogerpon-Wellspring and cannot safely preserve its 11% HP. Choice Specs Draco Meteor is the strongest attack and should KO an offensive Ogerpon from 88%; Terastallization is unnecessary and is more valuable for Kingambit later.

Ogerpon fainted; I must switch. Opponent has Dragapult (12%), Dragonite (15%), Gholdengo (14%), Ting-Lu (51%) — all low except Ting-Lu. Kingambit at 21% with 4 fainted allies has massive Supreme Overlord boost; Sucker Punch (priority) can pick off Dragapult, Dragonite, and Gholdengo at their low HP. But Stealth Rock on my side costs Kingambit 12.5% (~42 HP), leaving ~30 HP — still alive. Dragapult outspeeds and could finish Kingambit with any attack though; Sucker Punch fails if Dragapult uses status/U-turn etc.

Ribombee is faster than Dragapult (381 vs 142 base, max ~394... actually Dragapult max speed 383, Ribombee 381 — close, Dragapult likely outspeeds slightly). Ribombee takes Stealth Rock (12.5%, Sash broken), Focus Sash then useless. Moonblast KOs Dragapult at 12% if Ribombee moves first — uncertain.

Kingambit is the key: Sucker Punch priority reliably KOs Dragapult regardless of speed if it attacks. Bringing Kingambit now and Sucker Punching next turn is the best line; Ribombee is a fallback for Ting-Lu cleanup. Switch Kingambit.

Dragapult at 12% outspeeds Kingambit and can KO with any attack (Draco Meteor at -2 might not, but Dragapult often has Dragon Darts/U-turn). Kingambit has Supreme Overlord with 4 fallen allies (+40% power). Sucker Punch (priority) KOs Dragapult at 12% easily and hits super-effectively (Dark vs Ghost). Risk: Dragapult switches or uses a status move, making Sucker Punch fail — but the opponent's whole team is low; Sucker Punch is the only way to move first here. If they switch to Ting-Lu, I take no damage anyway. Sucker Punch is the clear play.

Dragapult’s -2 Draco Meteor is resisted and cannot KO Kingambit from 15%, while Dragapult is vulnerable to Sucker Punch. Full-health Kingambit safely absorbs Kowtow Cleave and preserves the strongest endgame position.

Kowtow Cleave is the strongest reliable attack and should KO opposing Kingambit at 15%. Our Kingambit comfortably survives either revealed attack, so there is no need to risk Sucker Punch failing or spend Terastallization.

Kingambit mirror: my Kingambit is at 15% and both Kowtow Cleave and Iron Head are resisted by Dark/Steel, doing only ~25% to their 82% Kingambit — no KO possible this turn, and their Sucker Punch/Kowtow will finish me. However, my Kingambit (Supreme Overlord +40%) is a crucial revenge killer: Sucker Punch cleanly KOs Dragonite (15%), Gholdengo (14%, neutral) and Dragapult (12%). Sacrificing it into a mirror I can't win is wasteful.

Ribombee is healthy and outspeeds everything; it takes 25% from Stealth Rock (sash breaks) but can threaten neutral Moonblast (Fairy is 2x on Dark, 0.5x on Steel → neutral) and Stun Spore to cripple their Kingambit, buying tempo. Preserve Kingambit's priority for the three sub-15% opponents and pivot to Ribombee now.
Ribombee quadruple-resists Dark, so Iron Head is the only reliable knockout. Kingambit comfortably survives any unboosted attack, and Terastallization is unnecessary.

Ribombee at 17.6% vs opposing Kingambit at 88%. Kingambit's Sucker Punch or Kowtow Cleave kills Ribombee regardless. Moonblast is resisted (Fairy vs Steel), does little. Sticky Web won't matter much against a slow opponent team already. Stun Spore is 75% and Kingambit still kills after. My Kingambit at 15% cannot survive either.

Best value: Ribombee likely dies this turn anyway. Options: Stun Spore to cripple their Kingambit (paralysis lets my Kingambit outspeed and potentially set up), or U-turn to bring Kingambit in—but Kingambit at 15% takes Kowtow Cleave and dies. Sucker Punch only works if they attack; if they Sucker Punch, Ribombee dies first anyway.

Stun Spore is the highest-upside play: if paralysis lands (75%), my Kingambit (Supreme Overlord +4 boosts from 4 fainted allies) outspeeds and Kowtow Cleave / Iron Head threatens. Their Kingambit would likely Sucker Punch regardless, so Ribombee is doomed; making the most of it means Stun Spore.

Ribombee fainted; the only legal action is switching in Kingambit at 15% HP. Stealth Rock will chip it further (~12.5% of 341 ≈ 42 HP, leaving ~9 HP). Next turn, Sucker Punch with Supreme Overlord (5 fallen allies = +50%) is the play against the opponent's Kingambit or any low-HP threat. No other choice exists.
Kowtow Cleave guarantees the knockout from 9% while easily surviving either opposing attack. Unlike Sucker Punch, it cannot fail if the opponent uses Swords Dance.

Kingambit mirror. I'm at 30/341 with 5 fainted allies — Supreme Overlord at max (+50%). Opponent Kingambit at 94% likely has Sucker Punch too; if they Sucker Punch, I die regardless unless I use a non-attacking move (Sucker Punch fails vs Swords Dance). But Swords Dance doesn't win me anything at 30 HP — any hit kills me next turn.

Speed: my 199 vs their base 50 — likely similar; speed tie or they may be faster. Kowtow Cleave is resisted (Dark vs Dark/Steel, 0.5x). Iron Head is neutral (Steel vs Dark/Steel: Steel resists Steel... actually Steel resists Steel, so 0.5x). Both resisted. Kowtow Cleave 85 BP vs Iron Head 80 — Kowtow better, but Sucker Punch (70 BP, priority) is the only move that guarantees I act first if they attack. With max Supreme Overlord, Sucker Punch does ~35-40% — won't KO from 94%.

I can't win this 1v1 realistically; best play is maximizing damage before dying. Sucker Punch guarantees damage if they attack (they likely will). If they Sucker Punch me, mine goes first only on speed tie/win. Sucker Punch is still the highest-EV chip to help nothing later, but it's the only move that reliably lands. Go Sucker Punch.
